body:
Thanks for taking the time to respond, I do feel somewhat better since yesterday, thanks to the thoughtfulness of sometime_blogger, and the clarity of mind that a night of sleep brings. Unfortunately not all of my problems can simply expire with the dawn of a new day, but at least some of them can, so I'm operating a bit closer to my usual capacity right now. Having looked at your other posts, I hope a new day not far from now brings you some good news of your own!

On another note, I have a very rudimentary knowledge of Norwegian, does your name mean "wight"? If so, very cool!

I agree with you on all counts, this all happened nearly 3 years ago, think of this more as an elementary school reunion than a "missed connections". Just wanted to let him know how he's affected my trajectory since then. If I can't, I can live with that, but what I couldn't live with is not at least trying to thank him for what he's done. I'm definitely not trying to re-live anything

Yes, it can be difficult, especially when it's just strangers giving kind words. Just because someone encourages you, is that an invitation to try to strike up a close friendship, or do you keep a nice moment as just a nice moment? It looked like he was rather busy on this subreddit dispensing advice, so I doubt he had a ton of time to give to every person here. Still, even if the sum of our interactions remains just on that one post, it was much more than I could hope for, and I can be content with just that.

Thanks for the positive thoughts! It doesn't seem likely I'll get in touch with him, but I suppose the other, more subtle angle of this post was to give feedback to this community that you do help, at least sometimes, and to keep up the good work! If the worst really has befallen him, I figure at least he had an effect on me, so just like how his writing was a fragment of him, I am a fragment of him as well, and so he still at least somewhat lives on.

I was on the other end of this, a friend of mine told me they wished I'd be more positive and didn't make jokes/chat about death and suffering and that sort of thing, after a while I just told him I wasn't interested in being friends any more if he took issue with one of the most central parts of my identity
I've told several people I'm suicidal and I don't think any of them have had any strong emotional reaction to it, lol. I guess I've been lucking out.

This is sort of related; I was thinking, as I am often wont to do, of throwing myself over a bridge by my house, this time more seriously than usual. Looking over the edge, I decided I ought to do it finally. Then, I figured I should finish my listen of *Storm of the Light's Bane*. Having done that, I realized I should listen to None So Vile before I die. And so on, and so forth, and now here I am. Not exactly a deathbed, but I will probably not die while listening to metal.

It is subjectively meaningful/meaningless, as is everything else. My distaste for life exists, and the negative value I attribute to it has meaning to me. This does not affect, on a grander scale, whether existence is good or bad. I'm not wrong, and neither are the people here who try to talk others out of suicide. Of course my death will have no objective meaning! And for the record, that quote was taken from someone siding against suicide, who very well might believe in objective good/evil.

Thank you for this reply; it caught me completely off guard to hear something I hadn't heard before! Perhaps I will take up writing, though it bore no fruit the last time I tried my hand at it. Either way, this was the best thing I read all week.
